newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty edges down vs basket, 1-day depos at lombard.
newsitem.headline: Zloty edges down vs basket, 1-day depos at lombard.

text.p: A late zloty rally caused by closing of intraday currency positions propelled the Polish currency near six-month highs set on Wednesday, dealers said.
The Polish zloty closed just under 2.7 percent from the trading band centre after morning losses pushed it down to around 2.55 percent from parity.

"There was a slight speculative currency-buying trend in the morning and then the zloty gained ground on position closing helped by dollar's slip against mark," said Mateusz Bieniek from Societe Generale in Warsaw.

The zloty closed down at 2.70/2.67 percent from the trading band centre against Wednesday's 2.74/2.71 percent. It closed at 2.8640/45 to the dollar, down from 2.8632/40 on Wednesday and at 1.8370/80 to the mark, down from 1.8341/47.
One-day deposit rates rose as the money market's cash shortage deepened, sending overnight deposits up to 24.80/25.10 percent from about 24.00 percent on Wednesday, dealers said.
They said December cash-outflows coupled with fast growing credit action absorbed funds and pushed up market rates.
Tomorrow/next rates closed at 24.80/25.10 percent from 24.30/24.85 percent on opening.

Some dealers said several big banks, which were usually lenders, were searching for cash from the beginning of December to keep the reserve positions squared and caused a slight panic among takers as liquidity dried up.
They said however there were no fundemental factors which would keep one-day rates at lombard rate levels of 25 percent for the rest of the month.
